title: On-foot blackout: screen goes all black within ~2-10 s of walking on a planet
description: BUG (owner-reported): after exiting the ship (disembark) and walking on a planet surface, the screen EVENTUALLY turns ALL BLACK — usually 2 to 10 seconds into walking. The DOM HUD keeps drawing (same signature as the space blackout fixed in TASK-75), so this is a render/camera/scene issue, not a crash. Repro: dock the ship on a planet (e2e flow from disembark.spec.ts / terrain-live.spec.ts), disembark (E), then walk (W) in a straight line; within ~2-10 s the 3D canvas is fully black. Suspected areas (starting points, not conclusions — reproduce first, then trace which background object the on-foot camera leaves behind or stops drawing): (a) the skybox/starfield camera-anchoring fix from TASK-75 (src/client/render/starfield.ts `anchorBackgroundToCamera`, called from the WorldManager frame closure right before render) — TASK-75 fixed the SPACE regime for the ship's chase camera; check whether the on-foot CHARACTER camera rig (src/client/camera/CameraRig.ts, the disembark handoff from TASK-27/31) gets the anchoring, gets a camera far enough, and whether the character camera's position/offset puts it outside the sky sphere or dome; (b) the atmosphere dome far-plane clip documented at src/client/world/WorldManager.ts ~line 96-97 (a BackSide dome beyond the far plane draws nothing → black) — the on-foot camera is much lower than the ship camera, the dome geometry may clip differently; (c) chunk streaming (src/client/world/chunks.ts, TASK-26) — check whether walking unloads/disposes chunks or moves a world root so the ground + everything falls out of the view; (d) the character prediction path (src/client/net/character-prediction.ts) moving the camera to NaN/off-map positions over time. Fix the actual root cause so on-foot walking of any duration keeps the scene visible.

steps.details: Reproduce in the e2e browser: dock + disembark (disembark.spec.ts flow), hold W, sample the canvas with the TASK-75 helper canvasRegionStats from tests/e2e/helpers.ts (TOP band {x0:0, y0:0, x1:1, y0..y1: 0.3} AND the whole canvas) every ~1 s and record the time of first all-black frame plus, at that moment: the camera position (expose or read via window.__SELF_SHIP__ / camera-debug hooks), the sky/stars/dome object positions vs the camera (starfield handles), the far plane, and the mounted chunk count (stream-debug). Pin down exactly which object(s) stop covering the view. Write a failing unit test for the specific defect (e.g. 'anchoring helper is applied on the on-foot rig' / 'dome not clipped at on-foot camera height' — whatever the root cause is) that FAILS before the fix.

Implement the minimal fix at the identified root cause so the 3D view stays fully drawn while on foot, for arbitrarily long walking, in every regime the on-foot camera can occupy (surface under the dome, and any atmosphere/space view if reachable on foot). Do not regress the TASK-75 space blackout fix (deep-space.spec.ts must stay green) and do not change the sky/star radii or renderOrder without a reason recorded in the commit. If the root cause is 'the anchoring is not applied in the character rig', apply it there (same one-writer-before-render pattern as TASK-77).

steps.description: E2E regression: walk for 30 s, never black
steps.details: New spec tests/e2e/onfoot-blackout.spec.ts (reuse fixtures + the disembark flow from disembark.spec.ts + canvasRegionStats from helpers.ts): (a) dock on the planet, disembark, assert the surface view is drawn (terrain visible, not black); (b) hold W for 30 s straight-line walking, sampling the canvas every 1 s; assert at EVERY sample the canvas is NOT all-black: whole-canvas mean luminance > 5 AND top-band bright-pixel count >= 10 (same thresholds TASK-75 used for 'not black'); (c) also sample at t=2 s and t=8 s (the reported 2-10 s window) and assert the same; (d) save .ralph/screenshots/TASK-88-1.png at t=15 s and LOOK at it: ground under the character, sky/dome above, no black frame.

cd app && npx tsc --noEmit; full npm run test; e2e: the new onfoot-blackout.spec.ts plus deep-space.spec.ts (TASK-75 regression), disembark.spec.ts, terrain-live.spec.ts, camera-handoff.spec.ts, self-ship.spec.ts, core-flow.spec.ts via npx playwright test --config playwright.e2e.config.ts <files>; eslint --fix + prettier --write on touched files. Commit fix(TASK-88): ...

acceptanceCriteria: On-foot straight-line walking for 30 s never produces an all-black canvas (e2e onfoot-blackout.spec.ts samples every second; mean luminance > 5 and top-band bright pixels >= 10 at every sample, including the reported 2-10 s window)
The root cause is identified in code (not papered over) and a unit test encoding the defect fails before the fix and passes after
The TASK-75 space blackout fix is not regressed (deep-space.spec.ts green, sky/star anchoring + far plane behaviour unchanged or explained)
Screenshot .ralph/screenshots/TASK-88-1.png at t=15 s of walking shows the ground and the sky/dome, not a black frame
npx tsc --noEmit green; full npm run test green; listed e2e specs green; one commit
notes: Signature match: TASK-75 (2026-10-06) fixed the SAME 'all-black canvas, HUD still drawn' symptom for the SHIP camera in space — skybox/starfield at the world origin left behind by the camera. This bug is the same family in the ON-FOOT camera regime: suspect the character camera rig never got the camera-follow treatment, or the dome's far-plane clip at character height. Verify before assuming.

The '2-10 s' window suggests a distance/position threshold (leaving the sky sphere / dome, unloading a chunk, camera offset growing), not a timer — look for what changes at that moment in the repro instrumentation from step 1.
The file/line hints above were gathered at planning time; re-verify locations before editing.
Do NOT commit pre-existing dirty .ralph/screenshots/*.png mods.
